transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m only here because my family made me come, but they’re the ones who are lying. They keep bringing out all these bank papers, right? Laying them all out on the kitchen table and pointing at the numbers, saying, look, it proves nothing was taken, the money is all accounted for. But they think I'm dumb. They really do. Just
Do you believe your family has stolen money from you?

Believe? I don't just believe it, I know it. I have known it for over a year now, clear as day. And it's not just my family, it's my friends too, they're all in on it together. They all sit there with those stupid bank papers I was just telling you about, acting like those printed out numbers mean something, like it proves nothing was taken. But I see exactly what they're doing. They are hiding my money. 

And they think they're being so clever about it, covering it up with all these... these fake expenses and excuses. Like, suddenly there's all these extra bills to pay around the house, right? Out of nowhere! And then my friend is suddenly asking for money for some big fundraiser, and my sister is talking about planning this expensive trip. A trip! Who just randomly plans a huge trip? I know exactly where that money is coming from. It's mine. They just shuffle my money around into the bills and the fake fundraisers and the vacation plans so I won't see it, but I see it. I'm not stupid. 

So yeah, I have to keep confronting them. I have to. I'm not going to stop, either. I don't care if they drag me to doctors like you or try to make me look crazy, I'm going to keep getting right in their faces every single day until they finally just break down and tell the truth.
Lately, have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Sleep? No, I don't know why you'd ask that. I sleep just the same as I always have. I ain't staying up all night or nothing. I need my rest, you know? Specially with all the stress they're putting me through. I mean, wouldn't you need your sleep if you had to spend all day fighting with your own family just to keep what's yours? 

So yeah, I sleep. I get my regular hours. Sometimes it takes me a minute to drift off, sure, just cause my mind is going a mile a minute, thinking about that so-called fundraiser my friend was talking about. Like, who even does a fundraiser for a community garden anyway? It's just a bunch of dirt and weeds! It makes absolutely no sense. But anyway, no, my sleep is regular. I lay down, I sleep, I wake up, and I get right back to watching them. 

They'd probably love it if I stopped sleeping, honestly. Then they could sit there and tell you, oh, look at her, she's not sleeping, she's losing her mind. But I don't give them the satisfaction. I get my rest so I can stay sharp, because if I don't, they'll just try to slip another fake bill past me.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Voices? Like, hearing things? No. No, I don't hear voices. I mean, why would I? I'm not crazy. That's what they want you to think, isn't it? They probably told you that before I even walked in here. "Oh, she's hearing things, she's losing her grip." But no, the only voices I hear are theirs. And let me tell you, I hear plenty of that. I hear them whispering when they think I'm not in the room. I hear the way their tone changes when I walk into the kitchen, you know? They get real quiet, real sudden. And then it's all, "Oh, hey, we were just talking about the weather," or whatever stupid lie they come up with. 

But actual voices? Like ghosts or something? No. I hear what's real. I hear my sister on the phone, talking real low, making those vacation plans. I hear the rustle of those bank papers when they're trying to hide them in the drawer before I come downstairs. That's what I hear. The sound of them lying to my face. And honestly, it's loud enough. I don't need to be making up voices in my head when the real ones are right there, plotting against me every single day. They just want you to ask me stuff like that so they can point and say, "See? We told you she was crazy." But I'm not. I just listen, real close, to what they're actually saying when they think I'm not paying attention.
Have you had any recent medical problems or head injuries?

Head injuries? Like I fell and hit my head and that's why I'm saying all this? No. No, I haven't had any head injuries. I ain't hit my head on nothing, I ain't been in no car accidents, nothing like that. My head is perfectly fine, thank you very much. I know exactly why you're asking that, too
Have you felt that you have special powers, special importance, or abilities that other people don’t have?

Special powers? What, like I can fly or read minds or something? No, no, I don't have anything like that. I mean, honestly, who do you think I am? Do I look like some kind of superhero to you? No, I'm just a normal person. I don't have any special abilities. I'm not important in that way, like on TV or whatever. 

I mean, the only thing I have is that I pay attention. I see what's right in front of my face. But that's not a superpower, you know? That's just having eyes and ears and not being an idiot. Anyone could see what they're doing if they just stopped and actually looked. But people don't look. They just go about their day, totally blind to the people right next to them who are trying to steal everything they have. 

But me? I watch. I notice when the mail has been moved on the counter, even just a little bit. I notice when the car is parked slightly different in the driveway, because I know they took it out while I was in the bathroom to go meet with that lawyer of theirs. I notice the way my sister breathes differently when she's lying. It's like this little hitch in her chest, right before she opens her mouth. 

Is that a special power? No! It's just survival! Because if I don't notice those things, they'll take everything. They'll take the house, the money, everything my parents left. So no, I don't have magic powers. I just have common sense, and I guess that's rare enough these days that people think you're crazy for having it. But I'm not special. I'm just the only one who sees the truth about what they're doing.
Have these beliefs that your family and friends are stealing your money been present continuously for more than a month?

More than a month? Oh, doctor, I wish it had only been a month. A month would be nothing. A month I could handle. No, this... this whole nightmare has been going on for way longer than that. It started, well, it started right around the time my income dropped. That was, let's see... it's been about a year and two months now. A year and two months of this constant, everyday stress. 

I remember it exactly, too, because it was right after I lost those extra hours I was getting. Suddenly I didn't have as much coming in, and you'd think your family would be supportive, right? You'd think they'd say, "Oh, it's okay, we'll help you out until things pick up." But no. That's exactly when it all started. The whispering, the moving my things around, the looks they give each other when they think I'm not looking. 

It's like they saw I was vulnerable, you know? Like they smelled blood in the water. Once my money got tight, that's when they realized they could start siphoning off what's rightfully mine. And it hasn't stopped for a single day since then. A year and two months of waking up every morning wondering what they're going to try to pull today. What paper they're going to try to forge, what account they're going to try to access. 

And it's exhausting, let me tell you. Just absolutely draining. Because you can't ever let your guard down, not for a second. If I take a nap, who knows what they're doing in the other room? If I run to the grocery store, they could be going through my drawers. So yeah, more than a month. A year and two months of having to be on high alert in my own home, with my own family. It's just... it's a lot, doctor. It really is.
Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way they can’t understand?

Hard to follow? Jump around? No, I ain't jumping around. I don't know why anyone would say that, because I speak perfectly clear. I lay it all out for them, A to B to C. Like, I'll tell my sister exactly what I know she did. I'll say, "I know you were in my room on Tuesday because I left a piece of thread on the drawer and it was gone when I got back." That's not jumping around, doctor, that's just giving the facts. That's a straight line. 

But you know what they do? They pretend they don't get it. They look at me with these big, fake confused faces, like, "Oh, what are you talking about?" or they tell me to calm down because I'm making no sense. But I'm making perfect sense! I'm just telling them the truth, and they don't want to hear it, so they act like I'm the one who can't talk right. It's just another trick. It's a tactic, see? Because if they admit they understand exactly what I'm saying, then they have to admit they're stealing from me. So they play dumb. 

I never lose focus. I stay right on the topic, which is my money and my things, and I don't ever lose my train of thought. I could talk about it for hours, straight through, and never get off track because it's my actual life they're messing with. So no, my speech is fine. They just don't like the words coming out of my mouth.
Aside from believing your family and friends are stealing your money, do you have any other unusual beliefs that other people say are not true?

Other beliefs? Like... like what? Like the government is watching me through the TV or aliens are coming down to get me? No, no, I don't have time for nonsense like that. I ain't crazy, doctor. I know some people out there think the earth is flat or whatever, but I don't pay no mind to any of that. I just focus on my own life, my own four walls, and what's happening right under my roof. 

Because why would I need to make up wild stories when the actual reality of what my sister and them are doing is bad enough? I don't have any other beliefs, if that's what you want to call them. Though I wouldn't call the stealing a belief, because it is a stone cold fact. But no, nobody is telling me I am wrong about anything else because I don't talk about anything else! What else is there to talk about? I don't care about the news, I don't care about the neighbors unless they are helping my family hide my cash. I just sit in my room and guard my stuff. 

My aunt tried to tell me the other day that I am just paranoid about everything in the whole world. And I told her right to her face that I ain't paranoid about the weather, I ain't paranoid about the mailman, I am just watching my wallet! I know exactly what is real and what ain't. So no, I don't have no other unusual ideas. Just the money. Just the things they are actually, physically taking from me. That is the only thing going on, and it is taking up all my time anyway, so I wouldn't even have the energy to worry about anything else even if I wanted to.
Are you still able to manage your day-to-day life, like taking care of yourself and handling your usual responsibilities?

Manage my day-to-day? Well, yeah. I mean, of course I do. I have to, don't I? Because if I don't take care of myself, nobody else is going to do it for me, especially not them. So, yeah, other than the arguments—because, believe me, we argue about the money all the time, like I said, it's a constant battle—but other than that, I still handle everything I need to. 

I make my own meals, for one thing. I don't trust them to cook for me anyway, not with everything going on. So I go to the store, I buy my own food, I bring it back, and I cook it myself. I make sure I know exactly what's going into it. And I eat just fine. I make sure I get my three meals, keep my strength up, because you need your strength when you're dealing with people trying to rob you blind in your own house. 

And I still get to all my appointments, too. Like, I have to go to the county clinic, right? And the assistance office to deal with my paperwork, since my income dropped and all that. I never miss those. I get myself up, I get dressed, I catch the bus, and I go down there and handle my business. I make sure all my forms are filled out, I talk to the caseworkers, I do all of it. Because if I don't keep on top of that, then I really won't have any money left for my family to try and steal, will I? 

And my things... well, I keep my things in order the same way I always have. Better, even. I make my bed every morning, I do my own laundry—I don't let them touch my clothes, obviously—and I keep my room spotless. I have to keep it organized so I know exactly where everything is. If I leave a pen on the desk, I know it's there. If I put my shoes by the door, I know they're there. So I'm very on top of my chores and my space. 

So, yes, I manage my life just fine. I bathe, I dress, I eat, I go where I need to go. I'm not sitting around helpless. I'm just busy. I'm busy doing all my normal daily things, plus having to do the full-time job of watching my back. It's a lot of work, doctor, doing my regular life and guarding my money, but I do it. I handle it all.
Have you been told by a doctor that you have any neurological illness, such as seizures, Parkinson’s disease, dementia, or a stroke?

Neurological? Like brain stuff? No, no, nothing like that. I ain't ever had a stroke or a seizure or any of those things you just said. Parkinson's? No, my hands don't shake, see? Steady as a rock. I need them to be steady, too, so I can write down my inventory every night. And dementia? Doctor, please. I just told you how I remember every single detail of where I leave my things. If I had dementia, I'd be forgetting where I put my money, and then they'd really have a field day, wouldn't they? 

But no, my brain works perfectly fine. In fact, it works better than most people's because I have to stay so sharp. I don't have any illnesses like that. The only doctors I ever saw before this were just for regular things, you know, like when I had that bad flu a few years back, or when I broke my toe kicking the door frame because I was so mad about my sister taking my twenty dollar bill. But nobody ever told me I had a brain disease. They'd probably love it if I did, my family, I mean. They'd probably try to get some doctor to say I had dementia just so they could take control of my bank account legally. But they can't, because I don't have it. I'm completely healthy in the head, doctor. Completely healthy. I don't have any of those things you just listed. Not a single one.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days in a row?

High? Energized? No, I don't get high like that. I mean, sure, I get irritable, but who wouldn't be? If you had people constantly sneaking around your room, going through your drawers, taking your hard-earned cash, you'd be irritable too, wouldn't you? It's not like I wake up and just feel mad for no reason for days on end. I get mad because there's a reason to be mad! 

Like last Tuesday, I woke up, and I was feeling fine, right? Just a normal morning. I got up, made my bed, went to check my lockbox—the one I keep hidden under the floorboard in the closet, not the decoy one on the desk—and I could tell someone had been in there. The papers weren't lined up the exact way I left them. So, of course, I got angry. I was storming around the house, yelling at my sister, asking her what she did with the fifty dollars I knew was missing. And she just looked at me like I was the crazy one, denying it, acting all innocent. That makes me irritable. It makes my blood boil, honestly. But it's not some random mood swing. It's a reaction to them!

And as for feeling energized... I mean, I have energy because I have to. I don't have time to sit around feeling tired when I have to be on guard 24/7. But it's not like I'm bouncing off the walls or staying up for three days straight painting the house or whatever it is people do when they're "energized." I sleep. I make sure I get my rest, because if I don't sleep, I can't think straight, and if I can't think straight, they win. So no, I don't have these weird moods you're talking about. I'm just a normal person reacting to a very stressful, very real situation where my own flesh and blood is trying to ruin me. That's all it is. Just regular anger at thieves.
Have you used methamphetamine, cocaine, or any other drugs recently?

Drugs? Meth? Are you kidding me? No, no way. I ain't ever touching that garbage. I mean, think about it, doctor, why would I do something stupid like that? 

If I was on drugs, I wouldn't be able to keep track of my money, would I? People on meth, they get all... they get all twitchy and they don't know what's going on around them, or they stay up for a week and then crash and sleep for days. If I slept for days, my room would be picked clean! They'd take the lockbox, they'd take my clothes, they'd probably take the bed right out from under me. I need my mind. I need to be sharper than a tack every single minute of the day. 

Plus, where would I even get the money for something like cocaine? Cocaine is for rich people on TV, and meth... well, meth is just dirty. And like I told you, my income dropped. I'm on assistance now. Every single penny I get from the county, I have to account for. I have my ledger, right? I write down the groceries, the bus fare, the soap... there ain't no line in my ledger for illegal drugs. 

If I spent money on that, or if I was getting high, my sister would notice immediately. And you know what she'd do? She'd call the cops on me. She'd love that. She'd probably go straight to a judge and say, oh, look at her, she's a drug addict, she can't handle her own finances, you need to put me in charge of her money. See? That's exactly how they operate. They look for any weakness. If I did drugs, I'd just be handing them the keys to my bank account on a silver platter. 

So I don't give them the satisfaction. I don't even drink, honestly. I don't take pills, no powders, nothing. I stay completely clean. I have to. It's like... it's like being a security guard, right? A security guard can't be getting high on the job if they're guarding a bank. And my job is guarding my own life and my own property from the people living right down the hall. So no, doctor, no drugs. Never have, never will. I am completely, one hundred percent sober.
Before this started, were you working, and did you stop working because of these problems?

Working? Well, I mean, I told you I get assistance from the county now, so it's not like I had some big fancy corporate job to lose. I used to do odds and ends, you know, cash work here and there, but... well, the real problem ain't about a job. If you want to know how this is ruining my life, it's about how everybody is treating me now. Just because I'm trying to protect what little I have! 

Like, take my bills. The electric, the water... things are tight. It used to be that if I was a little short at the end of the month, my aunt or my cousin might chip in, you know? Just help me out a little bit. But now? Now they completely avoid helping me with my bills. They won't even pick up the phone half the time! And you know why? Because every time we talk, I bring up the money. I have to! I have to ask them if they know what my sister is doing, or if they've seen my cash, and they just get all huffy and say they don't want to hear about it anymore. 

And it's not just my family, doctor. My so-called friends are doing the exact same thing to me. We used to do things together. Like, my friend Brenda, she's always organizing these little community fundraisers, or they'd put together these group travel plans, like taking a bus trip down to the lake for the weekend. But they stopped including me. Just completely cut me out. I had to find out from looking at pictures online that they went on a whole trip last month and didn't even invite me! 

When I finally cornered Brenda and asked her why, she actually had the nerve to say it's
Aside from the arguments about the money, have you had trouble keeping up with your usual work or daily functioning compared with before this started?

Well, no, not really. I mean, aside from the arguments—which, like I said, are completely justified because they are taking my money—I'm still doing everything I need to do. It's not like I'm sitting around staring at the wall all day. I have to keep my life running, right? 

I still handle all my own meals, for one thing. I go to the grocery store, I make my list, I check the prices, I cook my food. I have to be careful about what I buy now, obviously, because of the situation, but I'm still feeding myself just fine. I make a really good chicken stew, actually, and I still make that. And I get myself to the county clinic when I need to, and I never miss my assistance appointments. You can't miss those, or they cut you off, and I'm not giving anyone an excuse to say I'm not capable of taking care of myself. 

And my room? My things? I keep everything in order the exact same way I always have. Honestly, probably even better than before, because I have to be so meticulous now. I know exactly where my clothes are, my shoes, my paperwork. I have a system for everything. So, no, my daily functioning is perfectly fine. I'm just a person trying to live my life while dealing with thieves, that's all. I'm still me. I'm still doing what I've always done.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

See things? Like what, like ghosts or something? Or like, like hallucinations? No, no, absolutely not. I don't see things that aren't there. My eyes work perfectly fine, doctor. Better than fine, actually, because I have to keep them peeled all the time. 

I mean, if you're asking if I see things other people don't see, well, sure, I see the truth! I see what's really going on when everyone else is acting like everything is just perfectly normal. I see the little smirks my sister gives when she thinks I'm not looking, or the way the lock on my box looks just a tiny bit scratched, like someone was messing with it while I was in the bathroom. I see all of that. But I'm not seeing things that don't exist. Everything I see is completely real. 

It's actually kind of funny that you ask that, because my aunt—the one who won't help me with my electric bill anymore—she tried to pull that on me once. She was like, "Oh, you're just seeing things, nobody took your twenty dollars." And I told her, I said, "I am not seeing things, I had two twenties in that envelope on Tuesday, and on Thursday there was only one, and nobody else has a key to this apartment but me and the landlord, and the landlord didn't come in, so you tell me where it went!" 

People love to say you're "seeing things" when they want to make you sound crazy, you know? It's a very common tactic. They want you to doubt your own eyes. If they can make you think you're seeing things, then they can get away with whatever they want. They can walk right in, take my ledger, take my cash, and then just pat my hand and say, "Oh honey, you're just seeing things." Well, I'm not falling for it. I have 20/20 vision. I had it checked at the free clinic two years ago, and the guy told me my eyesight was perfect. So no, I don't see things that aren't there. I only see exactly what is right in front of my face.
Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

Put thoughts into my mind? Or take them out? What, like... like mind control? Or like some kind of sci-fi movie with people wearing tin foil hats? No, no, no, doctor. That's just silly. Nobody is putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are my own. They always have been. 

I mean, look, my sister might be a thief, and she might be incredibly sneaky about how she gets into my room to take my money, but she's not a psychic. She can't read my mind, and she certainly can't change what I'm thinking. If she could, don't you think she would have made me forget about the money she stole by now? She'd just zap my brain and make me think I spent it all at the grocery store on... I don't know, fancy cheeses or something. But she can't do that. She has to resort to all this sneaking around and lying because my mind is perfectly sharp. I remember exactly what I have and where I put it. 

And as for taking thoughts out... well, sometimes I might walk into the kitchen and forget why I went in there, but that's just normal, right? Everybody does that. You get distracted because you're thinking about how you need to check the lock on the window again, and you forget you went in there for a glass of water. That's not someone taking a thought out of my head. That's just being busy and having a lot on my plate because I have to be so vigilant all the time. 

It's actually really frustrating when people try to act like my thoughts aren't my own, though. Like, my cousin, he told me once that I was only thinking these things about my sister because I was stressed out. Like the stress was somehow putting the thoughts there! I told him, "Stress didn't make my twenty dollars disappear, Kevin!" But they just want to find any excuse to say my thoughts aren't real, valid thoughts. They want to say it's stress, or it's lack of sleep, or it's whatever. But it's not. My thoughts are perfectly clear, and they belong entirely to me. Nobody is tampering with my brain, doctor. Just my belongings.
Have you ever felt that people were sending you special messages through the television, radio, or internet?

Messages? Like... like secret codes on the news or something? No, doctor, definitely not. 

I mean, I watch TV, sure. I have this little flat screen in my room, it's not very big, maybe nineteen inches, and I mostly just watch the game shows in the morning. You know, to pass the time while I'm keeping an eye on things. I watch the people guessing how much a can of soup or a bottle of laundry detergent costs. Nobody on those shows is talking to me. They're just actors and contestants trying to win a car. The man on the local news is just telling me if it's going to rain, he's not sending me a special signal. 

And the radio? I don't even own a radio anymore. I used to have one of those little alarm clock radios, the black plastic ones? But it broke a few years ago. The dial just snapped right off when I tried to change the station, so I threw it in the dumpster out back. So I definitely couldn't get messages from that even if I wanted to. 

As for the internet... well, I have a cheap smartphone, but I don't even have a data plan on it right now. I can't be paying forty or fifty dollars a month for internet when I'm constantly having to replace the cash my sister takes from me. I have to pinch every single penny. So I only use the internet when I can get free Wi-Fi, like here at the clinic or if I go sit outside the library. And when I do use it, I'm just doing regular things. I check my bank account balance—which I check three times a day now, just to be absolutely certain nothing is missing from there, too—or I look up a recipe for dinner. 

I don't have time for nonsense like secret messages. Why would anyone on the TV or the internet care about me anyway? I'm just a regular person trying to hold onto the little bit of money I have. The only messages I get are the ones right in real life, like when I see my sister's car parked a block away when she told my mom she was going to be at work all day. That's a message, alright. It tells me exactly what she's up to. But no, nothing coming out of a screen. That's just silly.

I have to be careful about what I buy now, obviously, because of the situation, but I'm still feeding myself just fine. I make a really good chicken stew, actually, and I still make that. And I get myself to the county clinic when I need to, and I never miss my assistance appointments. You can't miss those, or they cut you off, and I'm not giving anyone an excuse to say I'm not capable of taking care of myself. 

And my room? My things? I keep everything in order the exact same way I always have. Honestly, probably even better than before, because I have to be so meticulous now. I know exactly where my clothes are, my shoes, my paperwork. I have a system for everything. So, no, my daily functioning is perfectly fine. I'm just a person trying to live my life while dealing with thieves, that's all. I'm still me. I'm still doing what I've always done.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent hallucinations in any sensory modality, which would favor schizophrenia or an organic psychotic disorder over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things that other people could not see), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
See things? Like what, like ghosts or something? Or like, like hallucinations? No, no, absolutely not. I don't see things that aren't there. My eyes work perfectly fine, doctor. Better than fine, actually, because I have to keep them peeled all the time. 

I mean, if you're asking if I see things other people don't see, well, sure, I see the truth! I see what's really going on when everyone else is acting like everything is just perfectly normal. I see the little smirks my sister gives when she thinks I'm not looking, or the way the lock on my box looks just a tiny bit scratched, like someone was messing with it while I was in the bathroom. I see all of that. But I'm not seeing things that don't exist. Everything I see is completely real. 

It's actually kind of funny that you ask that, because my aunt—the one who won't help me with my electric bill anymore—she tried to pull that on me once. She was like, "Oh, you're just seeing things, nobody took your twenty dollars." And I told her, I said, "I am not seeing things, I had two twenties in that envelope on Tuesday, and on Thursday there was only one, and nobody else has a key to this apartment but me and the landlord, and the landlord didn't come in, so you tell me where it went!" 

People love to say you're "seeing things" when they want to make you sound crazy, you know? It's a very common tactic. They want you to doubt your own eyes. If they can make you think you're seeing things, then they can get away with whatever they want. They can walk right in, take my ledger, take my cash, and then just pat my hand and say, "Oh honey, you're just seeing things." Well, I'm not falling for it. I have 20/20 vision. I had it checked at the free clinic two years ago, and the guy told me my eyesight was perfect. So no, I don't see things that aren't there. I only see exactly what is right in front of my face.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a prominent thought insertion, withdrawal, broadcasting, or passivity experience that would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or acute/organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion or thought withdrawal (schizophrenia symptoms), which are not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Put thoughts into my mind? Or take them out? What, like... like mind control? Or like some kind of sci-fi movie with people wearing tin foil hats? No, no, no, doctor. That's just silly. Nobody is putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are my own. They always have been. 

I mean, look, my sister might be a thief, and she might be incredibly sneaky about how she gets into my room to take my money, but she's not a psychic. She can't read my mind, and she certainly can't change what I'm thinking. If she could, don't you think she would have made me forget about the money she stole by now? She'd just zap my brain and make me think I spent it all at the grocery store on... I don't know, fancy cheeses or something. But she can't do that. She has to resort to all this sneaking around and lying because my mind is perfectly sharp. I remember exactly what I have and where I put it. 

And as for taking thoughts out... well, sometimes I might walk into the kitchen and forget why I went in there, but that's just normal, right? Everybody does that. You get distracted because you're thinking about how you need to check the lock on the window again, and you forget you went in there for a glass of water. That's not someone taking a thought out of my head. That's just being busy and having a lot on my plate because I have to be so vigilant all the time. 

It's actually really frustrating when people try to act like my thoughts aren't my own, though. Like, my cousin, he told me once that I was only thinking these things about my sister because I was stressed out. Like the stress was somehow putting the thoughts there! I told him, "Stress didn't make my twenty dollars disappear, Kevin!" But they just want to find any excuse to say my thoughts aren't real, valid thoughts. They want to say it's stress, or it's lack of sleep, or it's whatever. But it's not. My thoughts are perfectly clear, and they belong entirely to me. Nobody is tampering with my brain, doctor. Just my belongings.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent first-rank or bizarre psychotic symptoms beyond the fixed non-bizarre persecutory delusion, to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that people were sending you special messages through the television, radio, or internet?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of reference (receiving special messages through TV, radio, or internet). This is not covered by the patient's specific delusion (which is about people stealing her money/financial persecution) or any other item in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Messages? Like... like secret codes on the news or something? No, doctor, definitely not. 

I mean, I watch TV, sure. I have this little flat screen in my room, it's not very big, maybe nineteen inches, and I mostly just watch the game shows in the morning. You know, to pass the time while I'm keeping an eye on things. I watch the people guessing how much a can of soup or a bottle of laundry detergent costs. Nobody on those shows is talking to me. They're just actors and contestants trying to win a car. The man on the local news is just telling me if it's going to rain, he's not sending me a special signal. 

And the radio? I don't even own a radio anymore. I used to have one of those little alarm clock radios, the black plastic ones? But it broke a few years ago. The dial just snapped right off when I tried to change the station, so I threw it in the dumpster out back. So I definitely couldn't get messages from that even if I wanted to. 

As for the internet... well, I have a cheap smartphone, but I don't even have a data plan on it right now. I can't be paying forty or fifty dollars a month for internet when I'm constantly having to replace the cash my sister takes from me. I have to pinch every single penny. So I only use the internet when I can get free Wi-Fi, like here at the clinic or if I go sit outside the library. And when I do use it, I'm just doing regular things. I check my bank account balance—which I check three times a day now, just to be absolutely certain nothing is missing from there, too—or I look up a recipe for dinner. 

I don't have time for nonsense like secret messages. Why would anyone on the TV or the internet care about me anyway? I'm just a regular person trying to hold onto the little bit of money I have. The only messages I get are the ones right in real life, like when I see my sister's car parked a block away when she told my mom she was going to be at work all day. That's a message, alright. It tells me exactly what she's up to. But no, nothing coming out of a screen. That's just silly.

inference.note: Persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion >1 year with otherwise preserved functioning; repeated negatives for hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, disorganization, manic symptoms, substance use, and neurological illness make F20.0, F23.3, and F06.2 unlikely.

opening_question.intent: Find out the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a single, fixed persecutory delusion that family and friends are stealing and hiding her money, present continuously for about 14 months. The belief is non-bizarre in theme, persistent, and defended with conviction despite contrary evidence. There is no evidence of hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, disorganized speech, prominent negative symptoms, manic symptoms, substance use, head injury, or neurological disorder. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusion-related interpersonal conflict, which is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
